records.region: Southeast Greenland, Inland Ice and the exposed-rock coastal-margin belt southwest of Kangerlussuaq and Kap Edvard Holm.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Kangerlussuaq and Kap Edvard Holm are regional coastal context labels, not names assigned to the modeled river group.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The retained national original accounts for all selected geography but does not establish a representative named natural river or continuous surveyed surface/subglacial flow. Regional fjord, cape and ice geography cannot name this whole modeled group.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection opens in inland ice, first turns southward, returns northeastward among nunatak margins, then follows southeastward and eastward ice/exposed-rock terrain toward its actual lower-ice ending southwest of Kap Edvard Holm. No precise glacier identity or natural-river mouth is assigned.
records.completion_scope: Contiguous original pixels cover every selected part and join at ordinary source scale. The chosen opening, main reversal, intermediate ice/exposed-rock setting and actual terminal were inspected in clean enlarged views with private orientation aids. No material selected geographic interval remains unviewed.

component_scope_limits: Kangerlussuaq and Kap Edvard Holm are contextual coastal place labels and are not used as river candidates.
The source distinguishes ice surface contours, thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments; their intersection with the selected line does not prove flowing water.
No selected lake-throughflow, lake outlet, reservoir or managed-channel connector is established.
Historical thematic mapping establishes generalized terrain, not present glacier fronts, precise banks, modern hydraulic behavior or an ordinary river mouth.
A null candidate does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.region: Eastern James Bay, Québec; Jolicoeur corridor
records.material_pending_reason: The beginning of the selected northeastern opening is omitted from the regional originals. Its actual connection into the mapped southwestward reach, including any small headwater lake or wetland passages, remains unsupported. The potentially useful detailed RG 2001-08 source could not be obtained.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The mapped lower Jolicoeur corridor and its connected selected middle reaches; the unmapped initial headwater is excluded.
records.completion_scope: All24 parts were considered. The mapped downstream23-part corridor, intermediate joining settings, final northward turn and actual coastward ending are supported at ordinary corridor scale. The missing selected opening is a material geographic gap, not a requirement for exact banks or a whole-system naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Direct name support is strongest on the lower northward river. Upstream branches are geographically considered without assigning one hydronym to all of them.

scope_limits: The actual opening is not yet independently mapped in the inspected sources.
No single-name assignment is established for the complete modeled selection.
Regional generalized cartography does not establish every small wetland, present channel, tidal condition or legal name boundary.
The two CEHQ maps share base geography; they are not independent field-survey confirmation.

records.material_pending_reason: The selected Bull Canyon opening and eastward transfer into Deep Creek, and the lower wetland-to-Great Salt Lake through-connection, remain unestablished. The main named creek, reservoir passages and actual lake-interior endpoint are supported at ordinary scale.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Mapped Deep Creek corridor from the upper trunk through Holbrook, Stone Reservoir, Stone, Snowville, Rose Ranch Reservoirs and lower Curlew Valley. This is not an accepted identity for the whole selection, Bull Canyon opening, unestablished wetland transfer or terminal lake continuation.
records.completion_scope: All 39 parts and the actual Great Salt Lake interior ending were inspected in five original views. The named Deep Creek corridor and reservoir passages are supported; the two specified headward and wetland through-links prevent whole-route completion.
records.supported_name_scope: Mapped Deep Creek corridor from the upper trunk through Holbrook, Stone Reservoir, Stone, Snowville, Rose Ranch Reservoirs and lower Curlew Valley. This is not an accepted identity for the whole selection, Bull Canyon opening, unestablished wetland transfer or terminal lake continuation.

scope_limits: IDFG confirms Bull Canyon is a tributary of Deep Creek, but no inspected source establishes the complete selected headward opening and eastward corridor.
The maps depict the lower creek, adjacent lakes and wetland/lake-margin setting without establishing the full selected southward transfer into Great Salt Lake.

A long interior-lake continuation is not assigned the Deep Creek river name. Distinct named components or reservoirs alone would not prevent a representative system identity; the incomplete connections are material here.
Composite map shoreline and interrupted-channel symbols do not establish current water levels, discharge, operations, exact banks or formal hydronym boundaries.
No observation is drawn from discovery snippets, uninspected interactive maps or download links.

records.region: Northern Sonora, Mexico; selected inland-to-coastal route in the San Luis Río Colorado municipal region.
records.material_pending_reason: No original map pixels were inspected for the chosen opening, western and southern through-links, possible dry or managed passages, or actual selected coastal ending. Read municipal prose cannot establish those geographic connections.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No source-supported name is assigned to the selected whole route or to an individual selected reach. Municipal stream, canal and receiving-sea names remain contextual labels only.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research concluded with one source-material-pending primary state. Three exact source limitations are factual reasons and are not additional pending counts. No representative identity or completed scope-hold classification is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: No source-supported name is assigned to the selected whole route or to an individual selected reach. Municipal stream, canal and receiving-sea names remain contextual labels only.

naming_scope_details.no_unnamed_claim: Failure to establish a name in this bounded pass does not mean the selected feature has no local, Indigenous or official name.
naming_scope_details.natural_or_managed_continuity: Neither a continuous natural river nor a continuous canal/drainage route is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
